- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to sentiment-weighted forecasts.
- In 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 5–7 days); reduce forecast by 1–2% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model often misaligns with mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average of past 18 days.
